title: Safe Controller Synthesis for Nonlinear Systems via Reinforcement Learning and PAC Approximation
problem: Deep neural network control policies obtained through reinforcement learning exhibit good performance in simulations but cannot be applied to safety-critical systems due to lack of formal safety guarantees. Controller synthesis for nonlinear systems requires methods that bridge empirical performance and formal verification.
motivation: Safety-critical systems require provable safety guarantees in addition to good control performance, enabling the safe deployment of neural network controllers in real applications.
method: The method starts by training a neural network controller using reinforcement learning—a trial-and-error technique where the network learns to handle complex control tasks. It then converts this neural network into a simpler polynomial controller (a mathematical formula using only addition, subtraction, and powers of variables), which is easier to verify mathematically. The approach applies PAC learning (Probably Approximately Correct), which guarantees that the polynomial controller's decisions will stay within a bounded error margin with high probability. Finally, it generates barrier certificates—mathematical boundaries that formally prove the polynomial controller keeps the system operating safely.
key_novelty: The core idea is using PAC approximation (a mathematical guarantee about bounded errors) to convert an RL-trained neural network into a polynomial controller that can be formally verified as safe through barrier certificates.
contributions: Integration of reinforcement learning with PAC techniques for provably safe controller synthesis
Polynomial surrogate controller design with probabilistic approximation error bounds
Barrier certificate-based formal verification for nonlinear control systems
limitations: Computational complexity for very high-dimensional systems and runtime overhead of polynomial approximation not discussed.
primary_theme: Formal safety guarantees for RL-trained controllers via PAC approximation
